Manual Focus · Rider Panel

The Rider Panel: market research run on 200 AI cyclists living in the real UK

The Rider Panel is a simulated UK cycling market. Each of its 200 riders is an AI agent with a full life story, a home town and a budget. They live through the winter in their town's real weather. They see real prices and the real competition. Give them a product and each one decides week by week whether to buy it. Then they tell you why.

It gives a brand or product manager an answer in an afternoon that used to take months of fieldwork.

What the Rider Panel is

What the Rider Panel is: 200 AI riders connected to the real world around them

Each rider is an AI agent. It isn't a persona on a slide or a survey answer. Each one carries a written life with a job and a home. Each has money worries or none, a partner who gets a say and a goal for the year. Then we connect every rider to the same forces that shape real buying decisions. Your product is the only thing that changes.

Their own lives

Home, job, money, family, kit and riding goals. The mix of riders follows UK survey data. Each rider then gets a written life story with something happening this winter.

Every rider lives through the actual daily weather their town had over the same weeks last winter. Rain on the commute, frost on the roads, the windiest day.

Why it matters

Why it matters: research that needed months and a big budget, now in an afternoon

Asking real customers is slow and expensive, so most brands only do it for their biggest launches. Everything else gets decided on instinct. The Rider Panel makes testing a launch cheap enough to do every time, before you spend money on stock and campaigns.

How a study works

How a study works, in four steps

  1. Set up the world

    Load this season's real weather for every rider's town. Add the calendar along with every rival product at its real price.

  2. Describe your launch

    Your product, price, retailers and reviews. Write each version you want to compare.

  3. Let the riders live it

    Every rider lives the season week by week and keeps a diary. They decide whether to buy, when and why.

  4. Compare the winters

    Run a winter with no launch as the control. The difference between winters is what your decision changed.

The study

Study: launching a new folding smart trainer into a UK winter

To show the Rider Panel working, we invented a brand called Northfold and a product, the DD1. Northfold is not a real company. The DD1 is a smart trainer: a stand that turns your own bike into an indoor exercise bike. It is quiet and accurate. It folds flat to 14cm deep for small homes.

It launches in mid-November at £499, stocked by Sigma Sports, Tredz and Halfords with strong reviews. Every rival is real, at its real UK price and Black Friday deal. Wahoo's KICKR CORE 2 drops to £399.99.

Why the same winter is run three times

All 200 riders lived the same winter three times, from 14 November to 31 December. Each time, they had the same lives and the same weather. Every rival product had the same price and the same Black Friday deal. The only thing that changed between the three winters was Northfold. So any difference in what riders bought comes from the launch decision and nothing else.

Winter 1 is the control. Northfold doesn't exist, so it shows how the market behaves without the launch: who buys a trainer anyway and which brands they choose. Without it, you can't tell which Northfold sales are new buyers and which were taken from rivals.

Winter 2 is the launch as planned: £499 all winter, through the big retailers, with strong reviews. Comparing it with Winter 1 shows what the launch itself did.

Winter 3 tests a fix. In Winter 2, most riders who nearly bought said price was the reason they didn't. So Winter 3 makes one change, a £399 Black Friday price. Comparing Winter 3 with Winter 2 shows what that one decision is worth.

Follow one rider through the winter, week by week

Every rider keeps a diary. Each week includes the real weather in their town that week. Compare a rider who bought at £499 with one who only bought once the price dropped on Black Friday.

    Why people didn't buy

    Every rider who shortlisted Northfold and walked away told us what would have changed their mind. This is the most useful output for a brand, because it turns a sales number into a to-do list.

    Reasons are tagged from each rider's own words. A rider can give more than one reason.

    What to do next

    Actions: what the results tell Northfold to do before launch

    Each action comes straight from what the riders said. We tested the first one by running the winter again with a Black Friday price. The others are next in line.
